parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the decay constant $\lambda$ of the radioisotope.
hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in radioactive decay definition connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: Radioactive decay definition. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
$A = \lambda N \implies \lambda = A / N_0 = (1.3 \times 10^6) / (3.05 \times 10^{10})$; $\lambda = 4.3 \times 10^{-5}\text{ s}^{-1}$ (accept $4 \times 10^{-5}\text{ s}^{-1}$)
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Calculate the time $t$ taken for the activity of the sample to fall from $4.6 \times 10^3\text{ Bq}$ to $1.0 \times 10^3\text{ Bq}$.
hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in radioactive decay definition connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
Hint 3: Ensure all quantities are expressed in standard SI base units and verify your intermediate arithmetic before writing the final result to 2 or 3 significant figures.
parts.proper_answer: $A = A_0 e^{-\lambda t} \implies 1.0 \times 10^3 = 4.6 \times 10^3 \exp(-5.5 \times 10^{-7} t)$; $\ln(4.6) = 5.5 \times 10^{-7} t \implies t = 2.78 \times 10^6\text{ s}$; $t = 2.78 \times 10^6 / 86400 = 32\text{ days}$
